ambiguities:
[
  {"description": "Three distinct concepts are all called 'plan' by different stakeholders: the price plan (billing artefact), the feature bundle (product's meaning), and the sales-negotiated deal ('a third thing'). Only the first two have been modeled here (PricePlan and FeatureBundle). Should the sales-negotiated deal also be modeled as a separate concept, and if so, what identifies it and how does it relate to PricePlan/FeatureBundle?", "source_references": [{"lines": [87,89,285,287], "excerpt": "We've got two things both called plan, and the sales team calls a third thing a plan, which is the deal they negotiated, which frequently matches neither."}]},
  {"description": "Priya states an account 'has one active subscription per product' but Tom mentions a fourth product 'in discovery' that isn't finalized. Should Product be modeled with only 3 fixed values, or is the value_constraint premature since a 4th is anticipated?", "source_references": [{"lines": [71,73}], "excerpt": "Fixed today. There's a fourth in discovery, but I'm not going to pretend I know what it is."}]},
  {"description": "The 'Paused' flag overlaps confusingly with SubscriptionStatus ('If you ask the system for active subscriptions you get paused ones too'). It's unclear whether Paused should be modeled as orthogonal to status (a true independent boolean) or whether there's an implied business rule about which statuses can/cannot be paused. This is flagged as a known bug source but not resolved.", "source_references": [{"lines": [129,131,135}], "excerpt": "It behaves like a status but it isn't one, it's a separate boolean, which is exactly why it causes bugs. If you ask the system for active subscriptions you get paused ones too."}]},
  {"description": "The commercial/business rule for mid-term cancellation of annual subscriptions (run-to-term vs prorated refund vs credit) is explicitly left undecided by the participants. The system behavior (end date set to paid-through date, no refund) is captured, but whether this reflects the intended business rule is unresolved, and manual 'goodwill' credits happened outside the modeled system. No fact type for refunds/credits has been modeled since it was explicitly stated the system has no refund mechanism.", "source_references": [{"lines": [251,253,255,261,263}], "excerpt": "So the system rule is clear, and what's unclear is whether the system rule is the business rule. ... What happens commercially when an annual subscription is cancelled mid-term -- run to term, prorated refund, or credit -- is undecided."}]},
  {"description": "Priya states there is a denormalised 'current plan' field on Subscription maintained by the change process, separate from the change history, and that if they disagree 'the change history wins and the current plan is the bug.' This implies the current PricePlan on Subscription is technically derivable from PlanChange history (the latest effective change), yet it is also described as a stored field. Should 'Subscription has current PricePlan' be modeled as derived (like MRR) rather than a stored fact, given the stated derivation rule?", "source_references": [{"lines": [271,275,281}], "excerpt": "No, Sam, it does have a current plan field. The changes are the history, but there's a denormalised current plan on the record. ... And if those two ever disagree, the change history wins and the current plan is the bug."}]},
  {"description": "MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue) was explicitly confirmed to be derived (from price plan price normalized to billing period) and not stored anywhere, so it is deliberately excluded from the fact types per facilitator's instruction. Confirm this exclusion is acceptable and no derived-attribute fact type is expected for reporting purposes.", "source_references": [{"lines": [163,165,167}], "excerpt": "So it's derived from the price plan and the billing period. ... I'm not going to model it as an attribute of the subscription, then, because it isn't a fact anybody asserts -- it's a calculation over facts we already have."}]},
  {"description": "It is unclear whether Account itself has other attributes (e.g., a company name, contact, email) since Priya mentions 'company name absolutely not' and 'email is on the contact, not the account' -- implying a Contact entity exists that is out of scope but not modeled. Should Contact/Email be added to the model, or explicitly excluded as out of scope?", "source_references": [{"lines": [29}], "excerpt": "Company name absolutely not, we have four accounts called 'Acme.' Email is on the contact, not the account."}]}
]
